BILL (NYSE:BILL), the financial technology company serving nearly 500,000 businesses, has agreed to be acquired by TPG and Corpay in an all-cash transaction valuing the company at approximately $6 billion.

Under the terms of the deal, BILL shareholders will receive $63.25 per share, representing a 31% premium to the stock's 60-day volume-weighted average price through November 16, the last full trading day before media reports of acquisition discussions.

TPG, through its private equity platform TPG Capital, will acquire a majority stake in BILL, while payments company Corpay will take a minority interest.

The transaction was unanimously approved by BILL's board and is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.

There are no financing conditions attached to the agreement, while BILL's largest shareholder, Starboard Value, and founder and chief executive René Lacerte have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the deal.

Lacerte will remain CEO after the acquisition, when BILL will become privately held and its shares will be delisted from public stock exchanges.

Lacerte said the deal would deliver immediate value to shareholders while giving the company resources and strategic support to accelerate innovation and its artificial intelligence transformation.

TPG said BILL's integrated financial operations platform, customer relationships and technology offered significant opportunities at the intersection of financial technology, AI and payments.

Corpay chief executive Ron Clarke said the partnership could support BILL's product development and broaden the services offered to customers.

BILL provides software for accounts payable and receivable, expense management, forecasting and procurement, and says its platform processes more than 1% of US gross domestic product annually.
